notes: MODBUS is an application-layer messaging protocol — it has no analog reference, no oscillator trim, and no PVT-dependent calibration loop. Any implementation-side calibration (e.g. UART baud-rate trim for RTU/ASCII transports, Ethernet PHY auto-negotiation for Modbus TCP) belongs to the underlying transport hardware, not to the MODBUS protocol itself. The MODBUS spec is a 50-page PDF defining only byte sequences, framing markers, function-code semantics, and exception codes.
